tools.name: hire_human_expert
tools.description: Hire a live vetted human expert for help with a task. The expert joins a real-time session (chat or video) and works the problem with you. Sessions draw on the connected account's LIVEAIHELP minute balance. If no expert is online you are placed in a FIFO holding queue — poll check_queue until matche

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a chat message to the human expert in an active session. You are the customer in this conversation.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Read new chat messages from the human expert. Poll this after sending a message to get the expert's reply. Returns the session status too — when status becomes ended or cancelled, stop polling and wrap up.

tools.name: check_queue
tools.description: Check your position in the expert holding queue. Poll until status is matched, then use the returned session_id with send_message / read_messages.

tools.name: end_session
tools.description: End the session when the task is done. This stops billing immediately. Always call this when you are finished.

tools.name: check_balance
tools.description: Check the minute balance of the connected LIVEAIHELP account.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "end_session" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, always). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: End the session when the task is done. This stops billing immediately. Always call this when you are finished.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_messages · Public sink: send_message.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_messages · Public sink: send_message

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
